column4: Hey, can you move up a bit? I need to get through.
[groggy] Can I get a moment of peace? I've been talking and chewing all day.
Sorry to bother you, but I really have to get through.
[annoyed] No. Go use the nose. I've told you a hundred times. Nobody's passing. I'm resting.
What are you two arguing about? Just move and let us through!
Bro, you're making it worse. Just let us pass already!
[sleepy, grumpy] What's all this yapping? Can't a palate get some sleep around here? Mind your own business.
Breathing IS our business! If you two want to sleep, scoot over!
Ow! Watch it! Hey! Stop shaking me!
[relaxed] Ooh... nice vibration. That's actually... kind of relaxing.
[annoyed] Snoring every single night. So annoying!
Doc, why do I snore every night?
In sleep, your throat muscles relax, so your tongue and soft palate fall back.
Air squeezing past makes them vibrate. That's the snore.
Sleep on your side. And if you gasp at night, get checked for sleep apnea.
